# Sleep Log 2025

## Summary
I kept this log on the bedside table and filled it in each morning before getting up, which is the only reason it survived the whole year. Across the twelve months my average sleep came to 7 hours 20 minutes, a little better than last year and close to the figure I had been aiming for. My wake time settled at 06:40 most mornings, give or take the odd early start, and I stopped using an alarm at weekends to let it drift naturally. Time to fall asleep averaged 18 minutes, which feels about right: long enough to know I am tired, short enough that I am not lying there stewing. Bedtime moved around more than anything else, sometimes by the better part of an hour, and that is the thing I would most like to tighten. The log is plain, just the numbers and a word or two about how the night felt, and reading it back shows how much the small choices add up over a year. The best months were always the ones where the bedtime held steady, and the worst were the ones where it wandered, which tells me more than any single figure in the log. I stopped chasing a perfect night and started chasing a repeatable one.

## Log
January started rough after the holidays and averaged 7 hours 5 minutes, with several short nights in the first fortnight. February picked up to 7 hours 15 minutes as the bedtime settled. March held at 7 hours 18 minutes and the wake time began to fix at 06:40. April was the best month at 7 hours 35 minutes, helped by the longer evenings and more walking. May slipped to 7 hours 25 minutes when a work project pushed the bedtime later. June dipped to 7 hours 10 minutes, the shortest of the summer, with the light mornings waking me early. July recovered to 7 hours 20 minutes once the curtains were properly lined. August held at 7 hours 22 minutes through the holiday. September came in at 7 hours 18 minutes as the routine returned. October was steady at 7 hours 24 minutes. November slid to 7 hours 12 minutes with the darker mornings making the alarm feel cruel. December finished the year at 7 hours 28 minutes, with the time off giving me room to catch up. The range across the year ran from just under seven hours in the worst week of January to a little over seven and three quarters in the best week of April, so the swings were not as wide as they felt at the time. The time to fall asleep was slowest in November, around twenty-five minutes on the darker mornings, and quickest in the summer at about fourteen. Bedtime drifted latest in June and earliest in January, which is the opposite of what I would have guessed. On the whole the log shows a slow tightening rather than any dramatic change.

## Notes
Saturdays are the outlier, drifting 55 minutes later than the weekday pattern almost every week, and I have stopped fighting it because the lie-in seems to pay for itself. I cut caffeine after noon around April and the time to fall asleep dropped by a few minutes almost immediately, which was the single easiest change of the year. The last thing before bed is 20 minutes of reading, paper rather than a screen, and it has become the part of the routine I would miss most. The lined curtains in July made a genuine difference to the summer mornings. The one thing I have not solved is the variable bedtime: a late film or a good book pushes it back and the wake time does not move with it, so the following day runs on less. Next year I want a steadier bedtime more than a longer one. The one experiment that did not work was an early night on Sunday, which just meant I lay awake longer rather than sleeping sooner. The one that did work was keeping the room cool, since a warm bedroom added several minutes to the time to fall asleep every time. I will keep the log going next year, though perhaps a simpler version, since the numbers are only useful if I actually read them back.
